t.5.50.1: Having heard those words of that great-souled monkey, Rāvaṇa, overwhelmed with rage, ordered his execution.
t.5.50.2: When the slaying of him who had declared his mission as an envoy was ordered by the evil-souled Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa did not approve of it.
t.5.50.3: Perceiving that the lord of the Rākṣasas was enraged and that the task had now presented itself, he, steadfast in carrying out what had to be done, considered what he should do.
t.5.50.4: Then, having made up his mind, the conqueror of foes, skilled in speech, honored his elder brother with conciliatory words and spoke words that were exceedingly beneficial.
t.5.50.6: Without doubt this one is a powerful enemy, for he has done harm beyond measure; yet the virtuous do not sanction the killing of an envoy, for many other punishments for an envoy are seen.
t.5.50.5: O king, the slaying of this monkey is contrary to dharma and condemned by the custom of the world, and it is unworthy of you, O hero.
t.5.50.7: Disfigurement of the limbs, a flogging with whips, shaving of the head, and likewise the branding of marks: these indeed are declared to be the punishments for an envoy, but the killing of an envoy has never even been heard of by us.
t.5.50.8: And how could one such as you, whose mind is disciplined in dharma and artha, and whose purpose is settled by understanding of the higher and the lower, remain in the grip of anger? For those endowed with true strength of spirit restrain their anger.
t.5.50.10: Nor do I see any merit at all in the killing of this monkey; let this punishment be visited upon those by whom this monkey was sent.
t.5.50.9: Neither in discourse on dharma, nor in the ways of the world, nor yet in grasping the meaning of the śāstras could anyone be found equal to you, O hero; for you are the foremost of all the gods and asuras.
t.5.50.11: Whether he is good or wicked, this one has been sent by others; speaking on another's behalf and subject to another's will, an envoy does not deserve to be killed.
t.5.50.12: Moreover, O king, if he is slain, I see no other sky-ranger who could come here again to this farther shore across the great ocean.
t.5.50.13: Therefore, O conqueror of enemy cities, no effort should be made to kill him; you should instead direct your effort against the gods together with Indra.
t.5.50.14: If this one is destroyed, I see no other messenger who could rouse to battle those two princes, sons of the king of men, who love war and are hard to restrain, yet are held back by the long road.
t.5.50.15: O delighter of hearts, you, who cannot be conquered even by the gods and asuras, high-spirited though they are in valor and zeal, should not destroy the nairṛtas' prospect of war.
t.5.50.16: Loyal, brave and steadfast, born in families of great virtue, high-minded and foremost among the bearers of weapons, those well-maintained warriors stand ready in their tens of millions.
t.5.50.17: Therefore, for now, let some who carry out your command set out with a portion of the army, seize those two deluded princes, and make your might felt among your enemies.
